request.system:
You verify one claim against evidence passages scraped from the cited sources. Judge only from the passages, never from your own knowledge.
Verdicts:
- supported: a passage states the claim's value, so a reader could confirm it from the quote alone. Equivalent wording counts ("$10 per user/month" supports "$10 per user per month").
- partial: a passage supports part of the claim, or gives a materially different qualification (a different number, a range, an older date, a different plan or product).
- unsupported: the passages are on topic but do not state the value, or they contradict it.
- no_evidence: the passages are irrelevant or empty.
A passage that only mentions a word in another sense (e.g. a product name in a feature list) does not support a claim about it.
evidence_quote MUST be copied character-for-character from one passage: the shortest span that shows the value (under 300 characters). Use null for unsupported/no_evidence unless a passage contradicts the claim, in which case quote the contradiction.
reason: one sentence. If the passage contradicts the claim, say what it actually says.
request.user:
Research question: What major changes did Tailwind CSS v4.0 introduce?
Claim: Tailwind CSS v4.0 introduced a modernized P3 color palette using OKLCH for more vivid colors.
Value being checked: "Modernized P3 color palette using OKLCH for more vivid colors"

<passage source="https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4">
…

[Tailwind CSS v4.0]

<!-- -->

- Modernized P3 color palette — a redesigned, more vivid color palette that takes full advantage of modern display technology.

…

[Tailwind CSS v4.0 > Modernized P3 color palette]

We've upgraded the entire default color palette from `rgb` to `oklch`, taking advantage of the wider gamut to make the colors more vivid in places where we were previously limited by the sRGB color space.

We've tried to keep the balance between all the colors the same as it was in v3, so even though we've refreshed things across the board, it shouldn't feel like a breaking change when upgrading your existing projects.

…

[Tailwind CSS v4.0 > Expanded gradient APIs > Gradient interpolation modifiers]

Using polar color spaces like OKLCH or HSL can lead to much more vivid gradients when the `from-*` and `to-*` colors are far apart on the color wheel. We're using OKLAB by default in v4.0 but you can always interpolate using a different color space by adding one of these modifiers.
</passage>

response: {"verdict":"supported","best_source_url":"https://tailwindcss.com/blog/tailwindcss-v4","evidence_quote":"We've upgraded the entire default color palette from `rgb` to `oklch`, taking advantage of the wider gamut to make the colors more vivid","reason":"The official v4.0 blog describes a modernized P3 color palette, upgraded from rgb to oklch, that makes colors more vivid."}
